title: Telemetry curation and visibility pipeline for per-route cost & latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a nearline curation and visibility pipeline that canonizes runtime telemetry from streaming inference nodes and batch billing inputs into a single, queryable fabric that can emit per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns. This ticket focuses on the backend service that performs schema harmonization, event deduplication, KV-cache-aware attribution, and exposes an intermediate decomposition artifact for Console and billing consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry ingests streaming request traces and batch cost records into the curation topic with >= 99% schema validation pass rate
Normalized records include canonical fields: route_id, model_id, customer_id, tenant_shard, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_ms, kernel_ms, kv_cache_hits, request_timestamp
Deduplication reduces duplicated streaming traces by >= 95% in a noisy replay test
Decomposition service emits per-tenant per-route daily rollups and nearline minute-level deltas accessible via BigQuery and internal read API
End-to-end tests demonstrate parity with existing accounting for a sampled workload within 2% cost delta and latency percentile drift < 3ms at p95
Console can render the new breakdowns behind a feature flag without impacting runtime dashboards
implementation_notes: Two-stage architecture: (A) nearline curation service consumes raw telemetry topics, validates and enriches with model catalog metadata; (B) decomposition worker aggregates canonical events into cost/latency slices
Use schema-registry with evolution rules; reject unknown fields but buffer for audit to S3 for fast investigation
Leverage existing route->model mapping service but add a fallback heuristic that tags unmapped routes with 'unknown-model' and flags for manual reconciliation
Dedup strategy: windowed deterministic fingerprinting on request_id + truncated KV-cache signature; tune window to 60s for streaming bursts
KV-cache attribution: when KV-cache hit is detected, mark compute_ms as 'cached' and allocate cost differently per policy (configurable per-customer tier)
Emit provenance metadata (source_topic, ingestion_offset, ingestion_node, schema_version) for downstream auditability
Memory and throughput targets: sustain 40k events/s per partition during test harness; target 10s max processing lag for nearline ingestion
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Canary with internal tenant dataset (sandbox org) behind feature flag; run for 48 hours
Phase 1: Expand to 10 low-traffic customers and side-by-side comparison against legacy ledger for 7 days
Phase 2: Swap Console read path to new API for route breakdowns for 5% of users and monitor alerts
Phase 3: Full migration and deprecation of legacy replication pipeline after two weeks of stability
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for schema transformations and fingerprinting logic
Integration test pipeline that replays a 24h production trace into staging and compares rollup outputs with golden ledger
Load test scenario using k6 and synthetic KV-cache hit patterns to validate dedup window and latency budgets
Post-deploy verification dashboards: discrepancy ratio, processed_events_per_min, schema_error_rate, average_processing_lag
comments: 2026-02-12 @Ravi Kapoor: Started spike to evaluate fingerprinting approaches (CRC32 vs xxHash). Initial results favor xxHash for collision resistance at our throughput. Putting prototype in /git/pr/telemetry-fingerprint-spike.

2026-02-20 @Ava Martinez: Design review feedback: require explicit provenance fields and a retention policy for rejected payloads. Added to implementation_notes. Follow-up: security to sign schema changes.
2026-02-26 @Sofia Chen (PM): Prioritize coverage for dedicated customers who have custom routing policies; ensure policy flag flows into decomposition step. Moved this to Phase 1 of rollout.

2026-03-03 @Ravi Kapoor: Dedup window tuned to 60s after storm test revealed 30s undercounts. See internal playbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console-telemetry/dedupe-playbook and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/589

2026-03-08 @Security (review): Reviewed KMS usage for enrichment metadata; recommended encrypting provenance blobs at rest. Security review required for S3 retention of rejected payloads (tracking ticket SEC-2026-07).
2026-03-10 @QA Lead: Staging replay shows cost delta of 1.6% vs legacy ledger for sampled orgs. Latency p95 difference ~1.8ms. Marking as acceptable for Phase 0 canary.
notes: This implementation is intentionally conservative about schema evolution to avoid silent billing regressions.
We will expose a lightweight read API (/v1/rollups) that Console and billing workers can call; heavy analytical queries should use the BigQuery export.
Feature flag keys: feature.console.telemetry_new_pipeline and feature.billing.telemetry_new_pipeline
Consider follow-up ticket to add ML-based noise filtering to detect implausible tokens_in/tokens_out pairs
